routes.title: Technology route map
summary: From ore to your first power, your first machines and the next tier. Steel and the starter workshop are parallel routes, not a ladder.

groups.title: Mine and smelt tin and zinc
groups.text: Everything below starts with ore you can mine with a stone pickaxe and an ordinary furnace. Copper, iron, coal and redstone are vanilla materials.

steps.note: Tin ore breaks into raw tin; Fortune gives more. Deepslate tin ore works the same way.
Zinc goes into the machine casing and, later, brass.

groups.title: Bronze and the machine casing
groups.text: The first gate: every early machine is built around a Machine Casing, and the casing needs bronze. No powered machine is needed to make it.

steps.note: Mix by hand: three copper ingots and one tin ingot make four blend.
Smelting the blend is enough. The crucible and the Alloy Smelter are other ways, not requirements.
A casing is a crafting part: placed alone it is not a working machine.

groups.title: Your first power
groups.text: A generator, cable and one machine are enough to start. JE is electrical energy; JE/t is per game tick.

steps.note: Cable must touch the generator's power port and the machine's socket, not a decorative panel.
Burns coal, charcoal or coke. It stops burning when full, so no fuel is wasted.

steps.title: Power is flowing
steps.note: Fuel in the generator and cable to a machine: your first power source.

groups.title: Your first powered machines
groups.text: The Electric Furnace is the first useful output. The Crusher is optional, but it doubles what an ore block gives.

steps.note: Smelts anything a vanilla furnace can, twice as fast. Leave its output slot free.
The crusher takes the ore block itself: mine it with Silk Touch, or use a drill.

steps.title: A working production line
steps.note: Generator, cable and a powered machine working together. Expand only where it helps.

groups.title: The pre-electric workshop (parallel)
groups.text: The starter workshop makes plates, wire and alloys without power. It is a sideways route beside electricity, and its iron plates are what make steel independent of the generator.

steps.note: The hammer stays on the bench; each use wears it a little.

groups.title: Plates, wire and circuits
groups.text: The gate to the next tier: later machines need plates, wire and basic circuits.

steps.note: An unpowered way to alloy brass and bronze, instead of the Alloy Smelter.
The wire drawer is built from brass. The small crucible furnace makes brass without power.
Silicon comes from quartz; solder from tin and lead.

steps.title: Basic circuits
steps.note: Plates, wire and circuits: the parts every later machine needs.

groups.title: Steel, a parallel capability
groups.text: Steel needs no electricity: the coke oven and the steel foundry run on heat. It opens the heavy machines.

steps.note: Coke is a hotter fuel and the carbon for steel.
Iron plates come from the workshop bench or the metal press.
Piping in oxygen doubles the foundry's speed; it is optional.

steps.title: Steel
steps.note: Steel opens the arc furnace, advanced circuits and powered tools.

routes.title: Magic route map
summary: Casting, a magical workshop and transmutation are independent starts. Begin with any of them.

groups.title: Find something that glows
groups.text: Every magic branch can begin here. Luminous matter is an amethyst shard or glowstone dust; nothing needs a boss, a quest or electricity.

steps.note: Break amethyst clusters in a geode. Glowstone dust from the Nether also counts.
Glowstone from the Nether breaks into glowstone dust, which is luminous matter too.

steps.title: Examine a glow
steps.note: Sneak and use the shard to examine it. Your live First Light route shows what your research still needs.

groups.title: Casting: your first instrument
groups.text: Owning an instrument is enough to use it. Compose a small light spell first.

steps.note: Sneak-use the wand to open the constellation composer.
Studying at the bench is one way to understand First Light.

steps.title: Your first spell
steps.note: Kindle, or any spell you compose and inscribe. Spellcraft shows what you hold.

groups.title: A magical workshop: the first apparatus and Source
groups.text: Jug Nouveau is an independent start. The Imbuement Chamber works slowly without charge, so it needs no power to begin.

steps.note: Jug Nouveau's own spellbook, for glyph spells. The chamber below does not need it.
Archwood grows in its own forests in four colours; any archwood log works.
Your first magical apparatus.
Place an amethyst shard in the chamber. Ley Charge speeds it up; it is not required.
Links Source Jars, Sourcelinks and workshop apparatus.
Stores Source for powered workshops and helpers.

steps.title: Your first Source Gem
steps.note: Source Gems open glyphs, apparatus and helpers.

groups.title: Shared charge with technology
groups.text: A Ley Pylon stores Ley Charge for rituals and compatible apparatus. Fill it with Radiance from a Kindled Lantern or with electrical JE, so a technology player can supply a mage.

steps.note: 1000 JE make one Ley Charge; it never converts back.

groups.title: Transmutation without casting
groups.text: A separate specialty: no spellcasting needed. Learning and output permission are separate, so valuables stay protected.

steps.note: A later upgrade: Dark Matter is made from Aeternalis Fuel and a diamond block.
